fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The crowds come bringing "…the lame, the blind, the crippled, the mute, and many others…" and they lay them at His feet. And Jesus heals them. They're set right down at His feet, and that's where the healing happens.

Yes, baker, eat. Jesus says, "…they have already been with Me three days and have nothing to eat." He sees what the crowd needs, and He says it out loud to His disciples. Right after that He says, "I have compassion for this crowd…"
Nice try, friend, but clothes aren't the problem here. Jesus says the crowd has "…nothing to eat." That's what He tells His disciples. I've had a rough day or two, but I always found a snack.
Not quite, baker. Jesus doesn't say they have nothing to do. He says they have "…nothing to eat." He names the real need, and He names it first.

True, baker. Jesus says, "I do not want to send them away hungry, or they may faint along the way." He says it right after telling His disciples, "I have compassion for this crowd…" He's already thinking about what could happen to them along the way.

It's true, friend. Jesus says, "I do not want to send them away hungry, or they may faint along the way." The disciples hear it straight from Him. Just before that He says, "I have compassion for this crowd…"

Good guess, baker, because that's a very grown-up question. But money never comes up in this passage. The disciples ask, "Where in this desolate place could we find enough bread to feed such a large crowd?" Their question is where to find the bread.
Yes, baker! Matthew says, "And He instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground." Jesus gives that instruction to the crowd before the loaves and fish are even taken. Sitting down it is.
Close, friend, but kneeling isn't the instruction. The text says Jesus "…instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground." Sit is the word He uses.
Not lying down, baker. The text says Jesus "…instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground." Sitting it is.

No, friend. The text never says Jesus sends anyone for more. It says, "Taking the seven loaves and the fish, He gave thanks and broke them." He works with the seven loaves and the fish the disciples told Him they had.

Yes, baker! Matthew says, "…the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over." They all ate and were satisfied, and there were still leftovers to pick up. Any baker would love that kind of leftovers.

Good thinking, baker, but the text says something different. It says, "…the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over." That's seven basketfuls after they all ate and were satisfied. The text doesn't say who got them.

Nope, friend, no donkey in this passage. The text says, "After Jesus had dismissed the crowds, He got into the boat and went to the region of Magadan." I'd pay good money to see a donkey try to cross the Sea of Galilee, but Matthew sends Him by boat.
